items.headline: Top biotech deals in July 2026
items.preview: July 2026 saw significant M&A activity in the biotech sector, with major acquisitions and licensing deals.
items.article:
The third quarter of 2026 has kicked off with 12 major merger and acquisition (M&A) deals and eight licensing agreements in global drug discovery and development in July. Safe to say, interest in small molecules hasn’t waned, and cell and gene therapies and artificial intelligence (AI) continue to pull in investments.

Several multibillion-dollar acquisitions took place in July. American biopharma Vertex Pharmaceuticals’ first buyout this year was of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals for $10 billion. Crinetics developed paltusotine, a small molecule for acromegaly, which was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) last year. This broadens Argenx’s own autoimmune therapies pipeline, with Vyvgart having been approved in the U.S. and the European Union for myasthenia gravis.

Why this matters: These deals highlight the ongoing investment and interest in innovative therapies, particularly in the fields of oncology, autoimmune diseases, and mental health, reflecting the dynamic nature of the biotech industry.

items.headline: Why Western pharma is sleeping on China’s circular RNA revolution
items.preview: A new podcast discusses the potential of circular RNA in therapeutics and its underappreciation in the West.
items.article:
RNA therapeutics has had its defining moments, and the next chapter may be circular RNA. CircRNA is more stable than linear mRNA, longer-lasting in the body, and potentially re-dosable. Dr. Lu Gao, CEO of Therorna Inc., discusses the advancements in circular RNA technology and why Western pharma has not paid enough attention to developments in China.

Why this matters: Understanding the potential of circular RNA could lead to breakthroughs in therapeutic applications, and recognizing the advancements made in China may help bridge the gap in global biotech innovation.

items.headline: Clinical Development Expert has started
items.preview: EpilepsyGTx appoints Dr. Teresa Nunes as CMO to advance its gene therapy program.
items.article:
London-based EpilepsyGTx has appointed Dr. Teresa Nunes as Chief Medical Officer (CMO) to support the continued development of the company’s gene therapy program, including its progression toward clinical development. Dr. Nunes will be responsible for advancing the company’s lead gene therapy program, EPY201, for the treatment of focal refractory epilepsy.

Why this matters: The appointment of a seasoned expert like Dr. Nunes is crucial for navigating the complexities of clinical development and regulatory processes, which can significantly impact the success of innovative therapies.

items.headline: How Does the Cost of Stem Cell Therapy in Costa Rica Compare to the United States?
items.preview: Stem cell therapy in Costa Rica offers significant cost savings compared to the U.S.
items.article:
Stem cell therapy in Costa Rica typically costs between $5,000 and $15,000, representing a potential savings of up to 70 percent compared to the United States, where similar procedures can exceed $50,000. The lower costs are attributed to reduced administrative overhead and a more agile regulatory framework.

Why this matters: As patients seek affordable options for advanced therapies, understanding the cost differences and evaluating the quality of care abroad is essential for informed decision-making in medical tourism.

items.headline: Scientists map signaling networks driving disseminated glioblastoma cells in living brains
items.preview: A new study introduces INSIGHT to investigate glioblastoma cell signaling in vivo.
items.article:
A study published in Nature Communications introduces an approach called INSIGHT to investigate the signaling networks that guide disseminated glioblastoma cells while they are still inside living organisms. This method addresses the challenge of studying glioblastoma cells in their natural environment, which is crucial for understanding their behavior and treatment resistance.

Why this matters: Mapping these signaling networks could lead to more effective therapies by identifying vulnerabilities in the cancer cells, ultimately improving treatment outcomes for glioblastoma patients.
